newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds edge down as mkt nervous before jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds edge down as mkt nervous before jobs data.

text.p: German Bunds weakened moderately in early trade on Wednesday ahead of the release of German unemployment data for July which most analysts expect to show a modest rise on a seasonally-adjusted basis.
Dealers said the fate of the mark would continue to dominate events today, with fears persisting that the Bundesbank may raise interest rates if the German currency keeps sliding.
The dollar remained firm against the mark in early European trade where it was quoted at just below 1.88 marks.
September Bund futures, down seven basis points at 101.64 at 0710 GMT, were expected to trade in a range of 101.50 to 101.80 at least until the release of jobless data at 0755 GMT.
After that, the performance of U.S. bonds and the mark exchange rate would determine Bund movements, dealers said.
In the cash market, the benchmark 10-year 6.00 percent German government bond was bid at 101.96, down from Tuesday's close of 102.09, for a yield of 5.73 percent.
"People are incredibly focused on the mark," one dealer said. "But at the moment it doesn't look as if Bunds will go down further this morning."
Bunds on Tuesday spiralled lower for the fourth session in a row as the mark was battered lower against the dollar.
Overnight, U.S. Treasury prices closed slightly lower as the Treasury's 10-year note sale was awaited.

Analysts polled by Reuters on average expect a rise by 4,000 in Germany's seasonally-adjusted jobless total for July, with forecasts ranging from a fall of 15,000 to a rise of 10,000. The non-adjusted unemployment rates is expected to be 11.3 percent, up from 11.1 percent.

Dealers said a sharper-than-expected unemployment rise would dampen fears of a Bundesbank rate rise while a steep fall in joblessness could fuel expectations of a tightening and hit the short end of the debt market.
